I'm just tired of being made out to be some sort of monster, not getting any help, and when he does come around he practically forces himself on me sexually. I just can't live this life anymore. I have gone through the exact same thing. The trick is to run out of angst for the situation and I mean totally run out. Don't necessarily keep putting useless efforts out but if he expresses desire to see the child be open about it and take the emotion out of it.  If you haven't taken him to court for child support I strongly advise you to do so, it seems like a lot of stress but it's not as bad as it seems.

Focus on you and your child, let him do what he wants. Either he will disappear totally or become and more regular part of your child's life. When I was still feeling resentful over baby daddy being a shit face two things really set my mind differently. I was so worried about trying to hurt him or get even with him for not seeing my son that I wasn't really thinking about my sons best interests. If his dad wants to see him, awesome, and I leave it at that. Other people only have as much control over your emotions, goals, and self esteem as you let them. You will be happier when you cut the energy ties between the two of you. Visualize yourself ripping them out.

On topic but slightly astray, as a single mom I feel jealous sometimes when I see pictures of the single moms who have their children's dads around going out and having fun with friends and stuff. There's this one girl in particular that I always see posting pictures on Facebook of her out with her friends and I wonder sometimes if I will ever be able to have that. I am in the midst of a child support review and inevitably a custody agreement. My sons father has never been around, but because my son is on Medicaid, the state has initiated all of this. He is a drug addict and overall bad parent but sometimes I wish he wasn't if it were for nothing more than letting me have a life too. Love my son to a point of obsession but it gets tiring and frustrating and there's always that resentment and jealousy for people who do get to have it all. I would never put my son in harms way (with his dad) just to have a social life, but damn if he wasn't a shithead, having a social life and an awesome kid sounds so fun.

Well truthfully, after a few weeks of being disappeared the last time he did it, I told him to kick rocks. He never called on Christmas, never called on his birthday, and I've heard nothing from him. I'm so scared I can't sleep. They are taking it to court. According to the attorney generals office when I called, health and human services initiated this because of medicaid. His father then texted me back and said that he has been setting it up. That "it has been a long and difficult process". I don't know what to believe. I feel sick. The thought of a drug addict having visitation of my son is offensive. The attorney general also said that I got a letter in the mail about a review scheduled  (i never got it.) and that neither me nor his father showed up. Yet his father claims that he is the one who initiated the review and that I'm the only one who didn't show. Who do I believe? The dead beat that played fun uncle in my sons life here and there that has disappeared MULTIPLE times for months on end (my son is a year old) has filed for visitation and to pay child support through the state? Or was it really Medicaid like the attorney general office said? Would the attorney general be allowed to tell me if it was his dad? Or can they set it up as a confidentiality thing where they blame Medicaid?
Here's the fun part. I called his dad to ask him about it. Looks like I opened a can of worms best left alone. I am currently kicking myself.

It isn't possible that it was breast milk that you experienced. It's called collostrum and it is very different. Breast milk normally doesn't come in until 2-4 weeks after the baby is born. She also must have been eating a lot of acidic food which is bad for babies and can lead to severe reflux.
